research_mode: official GOV.UK primary statistical releases and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Release Scope
verified_claims: Quarterly fire and rescue incident statistics cover incidents attended by fire and rescue services in England for the year ending March 2026.
limitations: Attendance statistics do not measure all fires or emergencies that were not attended or recorded.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Source Transition
verified_claims: Fire data were collected through the Incident Recording System until November 2025 and through the Fire and Rescue Data Platform from November 2025.
limitations: A source-system transition can affect comparability and requires explicit period handling.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Incident Categories
verified_claims: Attended incidents are categorised as fires, non-fire incidents and fire false alarms.
limitations: The three headline categories do not provide an exact parcel-level hazard classification.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Primary Definition
verified_claims: A primary fire meets at least one criterion involving a non-derelict building, vehicle or structure, a fatality, casualty or rescue, or attendance by at least five pumping appliances.
limitations: The definition does not establish the severity of a specific property without incident-level evidence.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Secondary Definition
verified_claims: Secondary fires are generally small outdoor fires not involving people or property.
limitations: A secondary-fire label must not be assigned to an unobserved local event.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Chimney Definition
verified_claims: Chimney fires are fires in non-industrial buildings where flame is contained within the chimney structure.
limitations: A chimney-fire category does not prove building condition or future risk.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Weather Effect
verified_claims: Hot and dry weather can cause higher outdoor primary and secondary fire totals.
limitations: Weather-linked annual variation must not be interpreted as a permanent local risk change.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Highrise Definition
verified_claims: The release defines purpose-built high-rise flats or maisonettes as buildings of 10 or more storeys.
limitations: This statistical threshold is not interchangeable with every legal higher-risk-building definition.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire False Alarm Definition
verified_claims: A fire false alarm is an attendance where the service believes there is a fire but finds that no such fire exists or existed.
limitations: A false-alarm record does not prove malicious behaviour or equipment failure without its subtype.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire False Alarm Types
verified_claims: Fire false alarms are grouped as due to apparatus, good intent or malicious.
limitations: The subtype classification must not be inferred from an aggregate total.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Nonfire Scope
verified_claims: Non-fire incidents include activities such as flooding, road traffic collisions, animal assistance and assistance to other agencies.
limitations: A non-fire attendance is not itself evidence of fire risk at a parcel.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Nonfire Grouping
verified_claims: Recent releases group non-fire incident types into fewer categories based on existing FaRDaP categories without changing underlying definitions or coverage.
limitations: Presentation changes must not be mistaken for real incident growth or decline.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Collaboration Group
verified_claims: Collaboration incidents include assisting other agencies, effecting entry or exit, and suicide or suicide attempts.
limitations: Grouped collaboration counts should not be attributed to one component without detailed data.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Medical Group
verified_claims: Medical incidents include first-responder and co-responder categories.
limitations: Medical attendance totals do not measure the full demand on ambulance or health services.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Rtc Nonfire
verified_claims: Road traffic collisions attended by fire and rescue services are counted within non-fire incidents.
limitations: FRS road-traffic-collision counts are not the same population as all police-reported road casualties.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Fatality Definition
verified_claims: A fire-related fatality is one that would not otherwise have occurred without the fire, and statistical releases include records where the role of fire is recorded as not known.
limitations: The inclusion rule requires caution when comparing with other mortality definitions.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Nonfatal Definition
verified_claims: A non-fatal casualty is a casualty resulting from a fire whether or not the injury itself was caused by the fire.
limitations: The definition is broader than injuries directly caused by flames or smoke.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Live Revision
verified_claims: FaRDaP is continually updated, so published figures may differ from local fire and rescue service records and may be revised.
limitations: A published figure must be versioned and must not be treated as immutable.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Small Number Variation
verified_claims: Fire-related fatality counts are prone to year-on-year fluctuations because the numbers are relatively small.
limitations: Small-number changes should not be converted into precise local trend scores.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire Suffolk Underestimate
verified_claims: Suffolk fire and rescue service could not submit all incidents between September 2024 and June 2025 for technical reasons, so figures for that period are an underestimate.
limitations: Incomplete regional submission prevents exact local comparison for the affected period.
